sentence_en: After the clinical examination, we requested an orthopantomography as the first diagnostic test.

In it we can see how the wisdom tooth in question (38) is in close relationship with the NDI canal, detecting radiological signs determined as clear indicators of high risk of nerve injury during extraction maneuvers.
Thus, curvatures are observed in the roots , a darkening around the apices (mesial root) and an erasure of the upper cortex of the canal in contact with the distal root.
Although the orthopantomography showed us a fairly clear image, we decided to request a CT to properly plan the case before deciding on the therapeutic procedure.
In the CT images we verify that the contact between the wisdom tooth and the NDI is real and, therefore, the risk of damaging it during extraction is high.
In this situation, we inform the patient of the possibility of performing a coronectomy or partial extraction of the symptomatic third molar.
With this technique we aim to eliminate the symptoms caused by pericoronitis, since we achieve direct closure of the wound and the roots are included, preserving the integrity of the NDI.
The patient was informed of the possibility of an infectious complication of pulpal origin, which would force us to reoperate to complete the extraction.
Re-entry would also be necessary if, in the long term, root migration occurs, and these again generate symptoms of pericoronitis due to exposure.
Only, if this happens, probably the relationship of the roots with the NDI would no longer be so clear, nor would the extraction, therefore, be so compromised.
After obtaining the patient's informed consent, we decided to perform the coronectomy following the following surgical technique: Administration of antibiotic prophylaxis.
Making a bayonet incision and raising a full-thickness flap similar to that used for complete extraction of a wisdom tooth.
Making a cut of the crown with a fissure bur from the vestibular table, following an angle of approximately 45º.
This section is complete so as not to exert force on the roots with the lifters, which requires being very careful when approaching the lingual table so as not to injure the lingual nerve.
Subsequently, more dental tissue continues to be removed, with the same fissure bur or with a round bur accessed from the top.
The latter is a little easier than with the fissure bur.
In this way, the section is at least 3 mm below the bone crests.
This is intended to make it easier for the bone to regenerate on the roots and encompass them within the jaw.
The exposed root surface should not be treated.
Finally, the remains of the follicle are removed, without mobilizing the roots, the remaining tooth, and the wound is sutured with loose stitches that are removed in one or two weeks.
We must carry out radiological controls at one month, six months and annually.
All these steps were carried out in our case, and the patient has not presented any complications in one year after performing the intervention.

Given such data in the images, we decided to perform surgical exploration taking into account the possibility of being forced to remove the breast prosthesis.

At first it was thought that perhaps the fatty infiltrate could have entered the interior of the prosthetic capsule and pushed the prosthesis, without breaking it, creating a deep concavity inside, like a tunnel.

In the area of ​​the capsule that was in contact with the place where the fat infiltration occurred, there were no alterations, but we nevertheless decided to take a biopsy of the area of ​​injected fatty tissue; This biopsy corresponded in the histological study with fibrous tissue without signs of malignancy.

We decided then, once it was removed, to open it and send samples of the material that was inside.
The replacement of the removed implant was done with another one with the same characteristics.
The anatomopathological study reported the sample analyzed from the inside of the prosthesis as blood material.

sentence_en: SPECIFIC COMPLEMENTARY TESTS
Immunophenotype in peripheral blood: 45% of the total leukocyte count has an abnormal immunophenotype: CD45+, CD38+, CD138+, CD56+, CD19-, CD20-, CD5, CD10-, CD23-, Cd79b-, sIg-.
Bone marrow aspirate: Presence of plasma cells in a proportion of 50% of the total cellularity, of heterogeneous size, predominating elements of intermediate size.
Frequent binucleate and trinucleate cells.
Bone marrow biopsy: Multifocal interstitial infiltration of the marrow parenchyma by IG-Kappa plasmablastic plasma cells.
Medullary plasmacytosis of 40-50%. amyloid negative material.
Beta2-microglobulin: 7.3 mg/dl.
Bone series: No evidence of osteolytic lesions.
Immunoelectrophoresis in serum: IgG 4,390 mg/dl, IgA 14.5 mg/dl, IgM 4.17 mg/dl.
Immunofixation in serum: IgG-Kappa paraprotein.
Immunoelectrophoresis in urine: Light chain proteinuria (Bence-Jones) of 1,310 mg in 24 hours, for IgG-Kappa paraprotein and free Kappa light chains.
HBV, HCV, HIV serology: negative.

sentence_en: The intervention begins with the new tracheostomy and the preparation of the recipient vessels: facial artery and branch of the thyrolinguofacial venous trunk.

Afterwards, the scapular-parascapular osteocutaneous flap is dissected, and the donor area is closed, leaving aspiration drainage, and the left upper limb is immobilized with a sling.
The bony part of the flap is then adapted to the mandibular defect with ostosynthesis using the reconstruction plate placed in the initial intervention.
The skin part of the flap is folded as if it were a book, leaving one of the skin lobes intraoral and another extraoral (cervical facial).
The back of the supposed book is de-epithelialized and sutured to the remaining lower lip.
The intraoral part reconstructs the entire buccal mucosa up to the anterior pillar of the soft palate.
The external part reconstructs the left mandibular and submandibular skin area.
The posterosuperior region of the skin defect remains for dermal-epidermal grafting.
The blockage and dental splint are removed and the mouth is left "open."
Adaptation of the flap requires submaxillectomy and removal of part of the subcutaneous tissue in the posteroinferior area.
The anastomosis was made end-to-end from the scapular circumflex artery to the facial artery; and from the largest of the scapular circumflex veins to the thyrolinguofacial trunk.
The duration of the intervention was 14 hours; with an ischemia time of 2.45 hours.

One year after the intervention, upon observing a height discrepancy between the fibula and the alveolar ridge of the contralateral hemimandible of 17 mm, it was decided to perform vertical osteogenic distraction of the fibula by placing an intraoral alveolar distractor.
Distractor placement was performed under general anesthesia.

The fibula graft was exposed through an incision in the buccal oral mucosa, after which a subperiosteal dissection was performed to adequately visualize the underlying bone, taking extreme care to preserve the periosteum of the lingual surface of the fibula.
The intraoral alveolar distractor (MODUS ARS 1.5; Medartis®, Basel, Switzerland) was placed on the buccal surface of the fibula to correctly design the osteotomies.
Osteotomies were performed on the vestibular aspect of the fibula, using an oscillating saw, with saline irrigation.
A trapezoidal bone segment was thus obtained, having maintained the lingual periosteum intact.
The alveolar distractor was fixed with screws on both sides of the horizontal osteotomy.
Once the perfect functioning of the distractor was verified, it was placed in its starting position, in such a way that both bone fragments were in perfect apposition.
This is essential to initiate bone formation from the position of maximum contact between fragments and to achieve adequate postosteotomy hemostasis.
The vestibular incision was closed, leaving part of the distractor through the incision, in order to facilitate its activation.
During the latency period (10 days) the distractor activation was not performed.
After this, the same was carried out at a rate of 0.5 mm per day.
In serial orthopantomographic controls (obtained weekly) vertical distraction of the peroneal bone and the formation of bone trabeculae in the interface at the end of stabilization were observed.
17 mm of bone was obtained in 34 days, so that the fibula graft reached the same level as the contralateral alveolar ridge, with optimal correction of the initial height discrepancy between the two.
The consolidation period lasted three months, during which the distractor was kept in its initial fixation location.
Orthopantomography at three months confirmed excellent ossification between the basilar and the distracted fragment.
Subsequently, in a second intervention, the distractor was removed using the same intraoral approach.
The quality of the newly formed bone, verified macroscopically, was excellent.
In the same intervention, three 3.75 × 15 mm threaded titanium implants (Mozo-Grau®) were placed in the distracted area.

sentence_en: A 12-year-old girl with a history of prominent ears treated by otoplasty at age 8.
A keloid progressively developed in both ears one year after the intervention.
sentence_es: En ambas orejas se desarrolló progresivamente un queloide a partir del año de la intervención.

sentence_en: The keloids invaded the upper edge and posterior surface of the upper poles.
sentence_es: Los queloides invadían el borde superior y cara posterior de los polos superiores.

sentence_en: The right one had a horizontal size of 3.2 cm and a vertical size of 2 cm, and the left one had a size of 2.7 cm x 1.5 cm respectively.

sentence_es: La paciente no refería dolor ni prurito.

sentence_en: Excision was indicated given the large size of the lesions, with aesthetic and psychological repercussions.
sentence_es: Se indicó extirpación dado el gran tamaño de las lesiones, con repercusión estética y psicológica.

sentence_en: The intervention was performed under general anesthesia.

sentence_es: El tratamiento quirúrgico consistió en la técnica siguiente: se realizó una incisión en la cara posterosuperior del queloide, a partir de la cual de disecó un colgajo delgado de la cubierta cutánea queloidea, manteniendo un pedículo de unión a la piel normal en la cara anterior de la oreja.

sentence_en: After raising the flap of an adequate size, the rest of the keloid was removed.
The flap was sutured to the defect without tension.
sentence_es: El colgajo fue suturado al defecto sin tensión.

sentence_en: The size of the flaps was 2.5 cm x 1.5 cm in the right ear, and 2 cm x 1 cm in the left ear.

The surgery was associated with other treatments, commonly used to prevent recurrence: intraoperative injection of corticosteroid (triamcinolone acetonide) into the surgical bed, application of silicone gel to the resulting scars, and pressure therapy with an elastic band.

sentence_en: Silicone gel and pressotherapy were used for one year after the intervention.

The right ear flap presented a small suture dehiscence, which healed by secondary intention a few weeks later using topical treatment.
sentence_es: El colgajo de la oreja derecha presentó una dehiscencia pequeña de sutura, la cual curó por segunda intención a las pocas semanas mediante tratamiento tópico.

sentence_en: No necrosis or other complications developed.
sentence_es: No se desarrollaron necrosis u otras complicaciones.

sentence_en: A satisfactory repair of the defects was achieved, with restoration of the normal contour of the ears.
